title: Converting dollars to "cents" by multiplying by 100 is wrong for most of the world's currencies
assumption: Every currency has exactly 2 decimal places, so multiplying a major-unit amount by 100 always gives the correct minor-unit (cents) integer.

input.display: 100 * amountInJPY (0 decimal places), 100 * amountInBHD (3 decimal places), 100 * amountInCLF (4 decimal places)
input.description: A payments system that stores money as an integer and converts user-entered major-unit amounts ("¥1000", "BD 1.500") to that integer by hardcoding `* 100`, instead of looking up the currency's actual exponent.

what_goes_wrong: A ¥1000 (1000 yen) charge hardcoded as `1000 * 100` becomes 100000 minor units - but JPY has no minor unit, so the processor reads that as ¥100000, a 100x overcharge. A BD1.500 (1.5 Bahraini dinar) charge hardcoded the same way becomes 150 minor units - but BHD's minor unit (the fils) is 1/1000 of a dinar, so 150 fils is only BD0.150, a 10x undercharge.
why: ISO 4217 assigns each currency a number of minor-unit decimal digits, not a universal 2: JPY and KRW have 0, the dinars BHD, IQD, JOD, KWD, LYD and OMR plus TND have 3, and the two units of account CLF (Chile's Unidad de Fomento) and UYW have 4. A literal `* 100` bakes in the 2-digit assumption and mis-scales every currency that isn't one of the majority with exactly 2. `Intl.NumberFormat`'s `resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits` is a helpful hint but not an ISO 4217 lookup: V8 takes currency digits from ICU's copy of Unicode CLDR, which is display data and deliberately differs from ISO for some currencies. In Node 22 (ICU 78.2, CLDR 48) it reports 0 for IQD (ISO 4217: 3) and 0 for HUF (ISO 4217: 2), because those sub-units are not used in practice.
affects: any payment integration that hardcodes a decimal-to-minor-unit conversion

repros.expected_output:
USD 2
JPY 0
KRW 0
BHD 3
KWD 3
CLF 4
IQD 0
HUF 0
JPY 1000 buggy minor units: 100000 (should be 1000, no sub-unit)
BHD 1.5 buggy minor units: 150 (should be 1500 fils, not 150)

JPY 1000 buggy: 100000 correct: 1000
BHD 1.5 buggy: 150 correct: 1500

fix: Store each currency's minor-unit exponent explicitly, taken from the table your payment processor or ledger uses (normally ISO 4217, sometimes with processor-specific exceptions), and convert with `amount * 10 ** exponent` on an exact decimal value, not with a hardcoded `* 100`. Do not use `Intl.NumberFormat(...).resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits` as the source of truth for stored amounts: it comes from CLDR display data and disagrees with ISO 4217 for currencies such as IQD and HUF.

sources.title: ISO 4217 currency codes and minor unit data (SIX Group, official ISO 4217 maintenance agency)
Unicode CLDR supplemental currency data (digits used by ICU/Intl)

test_cases.note: their_function(amount, currency) that converts to minor units should return 1000 for ¥1000, not 100000.
their_function(amount, currency) should return 1500 fils for BD1.500, not 150.
